predecessors.name: Norman Italy
predecessors.text: the Norman realm of Roger II: Sicily, Malta, Calabria, Apulia and the duchy lands, without the Principality of Capua (Caserta block) and the Duchy of Naples

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: the island of Sicily and Malta, as Cliopatria's 1375 shape

ledger.x: 1130: Roger II is crowned king at Palermo.
1138: the royal army invades the Principality of Capua.

ledger.cp: Tripoli (ruler not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1148: Cape Bon, and Roger 'King of Africa'.

ledger.cp: African revolts (the page names no rulers)

ledger.x: 1266: Charles of Anjou conquers the kingdom.
1282: the Sicilian Vespers split the kingdom.

1283: Malta. In summer 1283 'an attempt by an Angevin fleet to relieve Malta was intercepted and defeated by Lauria'; the page does not say that Malta fell, but Cliopatria's island kingdom includes Malta from 1305. Page silent on the capture.
1296: Frederick is crowned king at Palermo.
1302: the Peace of Caltabellotta ends the war on 31 August.
1302: the island is recognised as the Kingdom of Trinacria.
1313: Frederick breaks the peace and takes Reggio.
1317: truce. 'A truce was concluded in 1317.' The page does not say whether Reggio was kept.

wars.name: Roger II's consolidation of the kingdom
wars.outcome: Roger lost at Nocera on 25 July 1132 and at Rignano on 30 October 1137 ('the greatest defeat of Roger II's career') yet absorbed Naples (1137) and Capua (1139); Innocent II was captured at Galluccio on 22 July 1139 and recognised him at Mignano.

wars.name: Sicilian conquests on the African coast
wars.outcome: Tripoli taken 1146, Cape Bona 1148; most of the African possessions lost to revolts in the mid-1150s, Mahdia to the Almohads in 1160.

wars.name: Hohenstaufen conquest of the Kingdom of Sicily
wars.outcome: 'the kingdom fell in 1194 to the House of Hohenstaufen': William III deposed, Henry and Constance crowned.

wars.name: Angevin conquest of the Kingdom of Sicily
wars.outcome: Charles of Anjou, offered the crown by the papacy, 'defeated Manfred at the Battle of Benevento in 1266 and in 1268 Conradin at the Battle of Tagliacozzo.'

wars.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers
wars.outcome: The island, lost to Angevin rule in March-October 1282, became 'an independent kingdom' at the Peace of Caltabellotta on 31 August 1302; the mainland became the Kingdom of Naples.

wars.name: Wars between Frederick III and Robert of Naples
wars.outcome: Reggio captured in 1313; a truce in 1317; an Angevin fleet and army 'defeated at Palermo by Giovanni da Chiaramonte in 1325'.

wars.name: Return of Maria and Martin
wars.outcome: 'In 1392 Maria and Martin returned with a military force and defeated the opposing barons'; the four vicars' baronial lands came back under the crown.

certainty.note: The mainland frontiers moved with the war against Capua, Naples and the pope until the Treaty of Mignano.
The October 1144 truce with the pope fixed 'the mainland boundaries'; the rest are sea coasts.
An island kingdom with sea coasts; the Calabrian ground of 1283-1302 and Reggio in 1313-1317 are contested and soft.
